reviewMetadata.sourceLessonFamily: Mathematical Habits and Place Value to One Million

learnerMaterial.title: Ten Times the Value
learnerMaterial.subject: mathematics
learnerMaterial.lessonGoal: Today you will use place value to explain why the same digit can be worth 10 times as much.
successCriteria: I can identify a digit's place and value.
I can write and explain a ten-times comparison.
keyPoints: Each place to the left is 10 times the place to its right.
Compare digit values, not just the digits.

vocabulary.definition: a rule that tells how two values are connected

sections.title: Follow the 7
sections.body: The digit stays 7. Its place changes, so its value changes.

sections.title: Worked example: compare two 7s
sections.directions: This page shows the complete example. No response is expected.

items.prompt: How does the value of the 7 in 70,000 compare with the 7 in 7,000?

steps: The 7 in 70,000 is in the ten-thousands place.
The 7 in 7,000 is in the thousands place.
The first 7 is one place left of the second 7.
Therefore, its value is 10 times as much.

sections.title: Your turn: choose the comparison
sections.directions: Choose one answer, then save it.

items.prompt: How does the 4 in 640,000 compare with the 4 in 64,000?
choices: It is one tenth as much.

feedback.correct: You compared the hundred-thousands place with the ten-thousands place.
feedback.incorrect: Locate each 4. Decide which one is one place farther left before comparing the values.

items.prompt: The 8 in 82,000 is how many times the value of the 8 in 8,200?

feedback.correct: You tracked the 8 one place to the left.
feedback.incorrect: Name the place of each 8. Then use the relationship between neighboring places.

items.prompt: Explain the relationship between the 5s in 50,000 and 5,000.

feedback.correct: Your explanation uses both place names and the ten-times relationship.
feedback.incorrect: State what each 5 is worth, then compare those two values.

sections.title: Reteach: build a place-value ladder
sections.body: Read the ladder from right to left: ones → tens → hundreds → thousands. Every left step multiplies the value by 10.

items.prompt: Which statement is true about the 3s in 3,600 and 36,000?
choices: The 3 in 36,000 is 10 times as much.
The 3 in 3,600 is 10 times as much.

feedback.correct: You used one left step on the place-value ladder.
feedback.incorrect: Put each 3 on the ladder. The farther-left 3 has the greater value.

sections.title: Check: make your own comparison
sections.directions: Use a fresh pair of numbers.

items.prompt: Write two numbers in which the digit 9 has a ten-times relationship. Explain your pair.

feedback.correct: Your original pair demonstrates the one-place, ten-times structure.
feedback.incorrect: Check that both numbers contain 9 and that the 9s are exactly one place apart.

whatYouLearned: A digit's value depends on its place.
One place left means 10 times the value.
A complete explanation names both places and compares their values.
